by: claude: tax back-fill 2015 onward, the four taxes the ten-year report reads (Belgium)
note: Belgium tax years 2015 to 2025 (calendar). These four taxes are national (Belgium sets only inheritance by region). PwC copies dated inside each year (last reviewed date in the note), the EY Worldwide Personal Tax Guide (content current on 1 July) where no PwC copy or explicit statement exists, Deloitte "Belgium Highlights" (as at January) for the wealth rows 2020 to 2024. The securities-account tax changed three times inside a year (March 2018 start, annulment from 1 Oct 2019, new tax from February 2021): each row is the rate in force on 1 January and the note says what changed; those rows quote the newest PwC copy, which states the whole history. Rows from 2026 were already on file.

rates.note: EY Worldwide Personal Tax Guide 2015-16 (content current on 1 July 2015): "In general, capital gains on assets that are not used for a professional activity are not taxable" (exceptions: speculative gains, sale of a substantial holding in a Belgian company to a non-EEA company). No PwC copy dated in 2015 exists.

Capital gains are not taxable to individuals realised within the normal management of their private estate (PwC, last reviewed 26 Jul 2016). 2016 ONLY: a 33% speculation tax on gains on listed shares, options and warrants held less than six months (from 1 Jan 2016; abolished from 1 Jan 2017). A portfolio held a year or more is not caught, so the headline stays 0.
Capital gains are not taxable to individuals realised within the normal management of their private estate (PwC, last reviewed 29 Aug 2017). The 2016 speculation tax was abolished from 1 Jan 2017.
